narrative:
The model estimates you have a 24% chance of failing your final year. While this is not a majority prediction, it is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses to strengthen your chances of passing.

The three factors that most influenced this decision were, in order: whether you receive extra educational support at school, your stated desire to pursue higher education, and the number of classes you have previously failed. 

Your lack of extra school support pushed the prediction toward failure; almost all students who passed did not need this support either, but in your specific profile the model saw its absence as a warning sign. Your answer that you do not want to continue to higher education was the second strongest factor and also pulled the outcome toward failing; every single student who ultimately passed had said they did want to go on to university. Finally, having failed three previous classes was the third most important driver and strongly increased the risk of failing again; students who passed had zero past failures on average.

To improve, you should seriously reconsider your plans for higher education, because that attitude appears to be lowering your effort. Speak to your teachers about starting extra school support immediately, and treat every remaining assignment as an opportunity to break the pattern of past failures. These steps can still change the outcome before the final exams.
